title: Dedicated capacity throughput calibrator and customer acceptance circuit
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Create a reproducible calibration harness and an acceptance circuit for Dedicated capacity throughput guarantees. The goal is to provide a deterministic way to measure throughput headroom, ramp behavior, and tail-latency under representative tenant mixes and to produce a customer-facing acceptance artifact that can be executed by SREs and Solutions Engineering during on-boarding.
background: Customers buying Dedicated capacity require measurable throughput guarantees and clear acceptance criteria before commit. Existing load suites are fragmented across teams (microbench, orchestra, pulsequarry) and do not provide a single canonical measurement that ties to billing, autoscaler behavior, and rollback safety. Recent incidents showed differences between synthetic and tenant-replay results when KV cache warmup and prefix variance were accounted for.
goals: (1) Deliver a calibration harness that produces a canonical throughput profile for a Dedicated pool. (2) Define a benchmarking methodology that ties throughput to autoscaler policy and SLA buckets. (3) Provide a runnable customer acceptance circuit and evidence bundle (graphs + artifacts) suitable for contract sign-off.
proposal: Build a modular harness (calibrator) that: generates tenant-mix traffic driven by configurable distributions; simulates prefix/KV-cache hit curves; runs ramp, sustain, and microburst phases with deterministic random seeds; and validates autoscaler behaviors (scale-up latency, max QPS stable windows). Output standardized artifacts: CSV timeline of QPS/latency, telemetry snapshots, and a signed acceptance report. Integrate with existing replay datasets but canonicalize inputs via a small set of canonical profiles (interactive-chat, short-gen, long-gen, embeddings-heavy).
acceptance_criteria: Calibrator can run end-to-end on a Dedicated pool and produce the canonical artifact in < 3 hours for 2-hour sustained windows
Measured throughput within 10% of expected headroom for canonical profiles across three different Dedicated sizes (S/M/L)
Autoscaler policy verification asserts scale-up latency and no oscillation for defined hysteresis settings
Customer acceptance bundle format documented and includes: raw telemetry link, aggregated CSV, percentile latency table, config used, and run checksum
SRE and Solutions Engineering have executed the circuit on at least two pilot customers and signed off
test_plan: Unit tests for workload generators and deterministic-seed playback
Integration test that runs a short calibrator profile in CI against a small emulated pool
Pilot runs against staging Dedicated pools with edge-case tenants (cold-KV, high-embedding fraction)
Full-run customer acceptance with Solutions Engineering producing the evidence bundle and customer checklist
rollout_plan: Phase 1: implement harness and canonical profiles (eng-only), land in bench infra
Phase 2: automate artifact generation and upload to bench-results bucket, wire to Console evidence UI
Phase 3: perform pilot runs with two customers and collect feedback
Phase 4: bake into Dedicated on-boarding flow and update sales contract template with standard acceptance language
telemetry: Token-level QPS and per-route latency percentiles (p50/p95/p99)
KV cache hit-rate over time and cache warmup curve
Autoscaler state transitions with timestamps and actor (policy vs manual)
GPU utilization, memory pressure, and scheduler queue length
risks: Synthetic profiles may still miss rare tenant interactions (complex tool calls) leading to optimistic throughput
Long runs needed for confidence may be expensive for staging customers—cost vs speed trade-off
Autoscaler instrumentation gaps could make verification flaky across fleet images
Overfitting acceptance criteria to internal fleets rather than customer workload diversity
mitigations: Include a 'stochastic audit' mode that injects rare tool-call patterns into 10% of runs
Rate-limit long soak runs and provide sampling-based shorter artifacts for quick sign-off
Add autoscaler telemetry contract tests as preflight checks for the harness
Maintain a rotating corpus of customer-derived profiles and require at least one customer-specific replay per acceptance run
